text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a spike in token-level p99 tonight on /api/chat-stream. Overall request latency ok but token TTFT shows large variance. Anyone see related kernel or KV behavior? :eyes:

ali: Confirmed, I pulled a quick probe for one node. TTFT p99 up ~320ms vs baseline 90ms for some routes. Decode time itself looks normal, but kernel handoff waiting in queue is high.

david: Can you paste the probe? is this on dedicated or hosted pool?
ali: Hosted pool, region-eu. probe snippet: ```
# probe summary
route: /api/chat-stream
sample_token_seq: 1..200
ttft_ns: histogram
decode_kernel_ns: histogram
kernel_wait_ns: histogram
kv_prefetch_ns: histogram
```

maria: That matches: kernel_wait is the culprit in a subset of requests. My hypothesis: batching heuristics caused a microbatch handshake delay when kernel selection falls back to the slow path.

jordan: Do we have metric names we can use in dashboards? I want per-route breakdown and tags for model, kernel, batch_size, kv_hit.

ali: Proposed metric labels and names: `redwood.token.ttft_ns{route,model,kernel,batch,kv_hit}` `redwood.token.decode_ns{route,model,kernel}` `redwood.token.kernel_wait_ns{route,kernel,reason}` `redwood.token.kv_prefetch_ns{route,kv_hit}`. Emit as histograms + cumulative counters for counts.

maria: For attribution dashboard we should compute: TTFT = kernel_init + kernel_wait + decode + kv_prefetch + postproc. We'll surface p50/p95/p99 and mean. Also add a panel for "% of tokens where kernel_wait > decode".

david: Agree. Two practical things: (1) sampling — we can't emit full token histograms for every token due to high cardinality; (2) roll-out tagging — we need to tag samples with `sample_reason` so we can bias for suspect routes.

ali: For sampling, suggest deterministic sampling by trace_id hash with per-route rate. Eg sample 1% globally, 20% for routes in suspect list. That keeps cardinality predictable.

maria: Example PromQL-ish aggregations for dashboard (pseudo): ```
# p95 TTFT by route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_token_ttft_ns_bucket{route="/api/chat-stream"}[5m])) by (le))
# fraction where kernel_wait > decode
sum(rate(redwood_token_kernel_wait_ns_count{route="/api/chat-stream",job="runtime"}[5m]) > rate(redwood_token_decode_ns_count{route="/api/chat-stream"}[5m])) / sum(rate(redwood_token_ttft_ns_count{route="/api/chat-stream"}[5m]))
```

jordan: Also want a "kernel chooser" pivot table: count by kernel version + avg kernel_wait_ns + kv_hit_rate. Helps spot if a particular kernel variant drives handoffs.

david: Ops concern: storing high-cardinality histograms (route+model+kernel+batch+kv_hit+sample_reason) might blow TSDB. Let's limit tags: route, kernel, kv_hit, sample_reason. Drop batch_size tag from TSDB and compute batch-size buckets offline from trace logs.

ali: For immediate triage I've pushed a small runtime patch that tags tokens with `sample_reason=ttft_probe` for 10% of requests on /api/chat-stream. Deploy bot: ```deploy-bot: deployed runtime@edge-2026-03-18-ttft-probe to region-eu```.

maria: Nice. Can we also add a lightweight flame trace that captures kernel queue timestamps for sampled tokens? Even a 6-field microtrace helps.

ali: Yeah we emit microtrace as a compact JSON blob to tracing backend only for sampled tokens. Fields: trace_id, token_idx, ts_kernel_enqueued, ts_kernel_start, ts_kernel_end, kv_hit. Example payload: ```{"trace_id":"abc","token":3,"enq":167, "start":489, "end":620, "kv":true}```

jordan: For dashboard UX: top row = route selector + model selector, middle row = TTFT p50/p95/p99 heatmap by kernel, bottom row = trace sample table with link to full trace, and right rail = alerts (p99_TTFT > 250ms for 5m).

david: Action items: 1) ali will keep probe running and increase sample to 20% if noise persists (due EOD). 2) maria will create Grafana dashboard skeleton and wire the panels. 3) jordan will add kernel-chooser pivot panel. 4) ops will set temporary alert (p99 TTFT > 250ms).

ali: I started a short-lived tag: `ttft-investigations/3612345678` on Prometheus metrics to be able to filter.

maria: If probe shows consistent kernel_wait outliers pinned to a specific kernel, we'll coordinate a canary rollback of that kernel version.

ops-bot: :information_source: incident-tracker created ticket #INF-472: "token-level TTFT spike — kernel_wait outliers" assigned to ali.

jordan: Thanks all. I'll mock the dashboard tomorrow morning and post a screenshot. :thumbsup:

maria: closing loop — keep the probe on for 6 hours, then we'll evaluate and decide whether to expand sampling or dig into scheduler heuristics.
